# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 3, 2026
1 4:50a ○ JSONStorage kwargs path and existing sort_keys usage located
2 " ○ JSONStorage.write serializes via json.dumps with stored kwargs
3 " ◆ JSONStorage now defaults to sorted keys
4 " ○ Test run failed on unrecognized pytest-cov arguments
5 " ● Removed meaningless assertion from sort_keys default test
6 " ✓ Sorted-key default for JSONStorage left uncommitted
7 " ○ sort_keys=True breaks inserts with mixed int and str dict keys
8 " ✓ Uncommitted sort_keys work reverted in tinydb working tree
9 4:53a ⚷ JSONStorage kwargs are documented as forwarded to json.dumps with a callable-safety warning
10 4:54a ◆ JSONStorage defaults to sorted keys with sort_keys=False opt-out and new tests
S1 Make JSONStorage write JSON keys sorted by default while keeping sort_keys=False as an opt-out, with tests. Also surfaced: the default breaks inserts for dicts with mixed int and str keys. (Nov 3, 4:54 AM)
**Investigated**: The primary session located the JSONStorage kwargs path in tinydb/storages.py, where write() calls json.dumps with the stored kwargs. It also checked the existing sort_keys usage in tests/test_storages.py (test_json_kwargs) and docs/usage.rst, and read the kwargs safety warnings in the constructor docstring and usage docs.

**Learned**: JSONStorage forwards all extra constructor kwargs to json.dumps on every write, and the docs warn that callable kwargs such as default or cls run on every write. Sorting keys by default raises TypeError when a dict mixes int and str keys: inserting {'m': {1: 'a', 'b': 2}} fails with "'<' not supported between 'str' and 'int'". Before the change, that insert succeeded and the int key was written as a string.

**Completed**: In tinydb/storages.py, JSONStorage.__init__ now calls kwargs.setdefault('sort_keys', True), and its docstring documents the default and the sort_keys=False opt-out. In tests/test_storages.py, test_json_sort_keys_default and test_json_sort_keys_disabled were added. The full suite passes with 230 tests. The change is uncommitted in the working tree.

**Next Steps**: The session has not yet decided how to handle the mixed-key regression. The primary session offered two options: fall back to unsorted output when sort_keys was not set explicitly and sorting raises TypeError, or keep the breaking change and note it in the changelog. docs/usage.rst still passes sort_keys=True explicitly in its example. That is now redundant but harmless and has not been changed.

**Notes**: The primary session suspects an earlier attempt at this change was reverted because of the same mixed-key failure, but it did not confirm that. The sorted-key default is a behavior change for any caller relying on insertion order in the JSON file, and it is not yet committed. The suite passing does not cover the mixed-key case, since no test exercises it.
